In 2024, VirtueVigil scored 91 films using the VVWS dual-scoring system. The results are below in full. This is not a curated highlight reel. It is every 2024 film we reviewed, ranked from highest to lowest woke score. No edits. No omissions. The complete picture.

The Woke Score measures the density and intensity of progressive ideological content across categories including gender politics, religious critique, racial messaging, sexual content framing, and institutional authority. A higher score means more of that content, delivered with greater intensity. The Traditional Score measures countervailing content: individual agency, faith, family, earned virtue, and consequence-based storytelling. The Score Margin tells you which direction the film leans and by how much.

You will find Best Picture winners, box office disasters, prestige acquisitions, and franchise sequels on this list. Some of the highest-scoring films are technically accomplished. Some are not. The scoring system does not care about craftsmanship. It measures ideology. Use the individual reviews for the full picture on quality, storytelling, and whether a given film is worth your time.

Full reviews are available for every film listed. Click any title to read the complete VirtueVigil analysis, including the trope audit, creative team profile, and parental guidance assessment.

#1 — Conclave (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE WOKE: 42.6 TRAD: 3.85 MARGIN: -39 WOKE

Genre: Thriller • Platform: Streaming

Edward Berger's Conclave is the highest woke-scoring 2024 film in the VirtueVigil database. That distinction matters precisely because this is not a cheap or careless film. It is a visually sumptuous, masterfully acted Vatican political thriller that uses its prestige execution to deliver a sustained progressive theological argument. Ralph Fiennes leads an ensemble of cardinals maneuvering for power, while the script quietly builds its case that institutional religious certainty is the enemy of moral progress. The twist ending, centering an intersex character in the papal succession, is the film's ideological climax delivered after more than 100 minutes of earned goodwill. A Woke Trap by every VirtueVigil definition: the agenda reveals itself only after the viewer is fully invested. Eight Oscar nominations followed.

#2 — Heretic (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE WOKE: 41.0 TRAD: 14.0 MARGIN: -27 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Streaming

Heretic is not a horror film that happens to include religion. It is a theological assault on Christianity and all monotheistic faith delivered via Hugh Grant's most charming and most dangerous screen performance. Two Mormon missionaries are invited into a soft-spoken man's home. What follows is an extended, methodical dismantling of religious belief using logic, manipulation, and film theory. Grant's Mr. Reed argues that all religion is a control system, prayer is statistically worthless, and Jesus is a remix of older myths. The missionaries are sympathetic. They are also outmatched. Scott Beck and Bryan Woods constructed a philosophical trap as airtight as the physical one. One of the most ideologically committed films of the year and one of the most skillfully executed.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Heretic

#3 — The Substance (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE WOKE: 37.0 TRAD: 13.0 MARGIN: -24 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Streaming

Coralie Fargeat delivered a body horror film about a fading TV star who uses a black-market drug to create a younger version of herself, and used every frame as a statement about how the entertainment industry consumes women. Demi Moore gives a career-redefining vanity-free performance. The body horror is the ideology made physical: beauty standards as violence, the male gaze as weapon. Fargeat turns the camera against the viewer in sequences designed to make complicity visible. This is not allegory masquerading as entertainment. It is a feminist argument in Cronenbergian packaging, open about its thesis from the first scene, consistent through the grotesque finale. One of the year's most technically accomplished and most deliberately ideological films.

#4 — Anora (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE WOKE: 36.0 TRAD: 10.0 MARGIN: -26 WOKE

Genre: Drama • Platform: Streaming

Sean Baker won Best Picture at the 97th Academy Awards for this story of a Brooklyn sex worker whose whirlwind marriage to a Russian oligarch's son collapses when his family intervenes. Baker dedicated his Oscar to sex workers everywhere. The film's progressive framework is embedded in its naturalistic storytelling so completely that it does not need to announce itself: the sex work is presented without moral judgment, class structures are interrogated, and the ending refuses redemption through conventional means. The Palme d'Or at Cannes came first. The Academy followed. Anora is the market leader for 2024 prestige progressivism delivered without the taste of a lecture.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Anora

#5 — MaXXXine (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 32.0 TRAD: 14.0 MARGIN: -18 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Theatrical

Ti West closed his X trilogy with a film set in 1985 Hollywood that simultaneously functions as a feminist manifesto and a sustained attack on the religious right. The Night Stalker stalks the streets. A televangelist villain connects conservative moral authority to serial murder. Every male character is predatory, incompetent, or both. Maxine Minx's survival and eventual triumph is framed as righteous defiance against every institution that tried to define her. West's craft is what elevates this above a standard genre film: the ideological content is so embedded in the aesthetic that it feels like genre convention rather than political lecture. That integration is precisely why the woke score is as high as it is.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of MaXXXine

#6 — Immaculate (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE WOKE: 29.0 TRAD: 8.0 MARGIN: -21 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Theatrical / Hulu

Sydney Sweeney spent years developing Immaculate specifically as a vehicle for its reproductive rights message, and the film that emerged is one of the most precisely crafted ideological horror films of the year. An American nun discovers she has been impregnated without consent at an Italian convent. Every element of the Catholic setting is repurposed as a symbol of institutional control over women's bodies. The nuns who enforce the convent's rules are complicit in that control. The ending is among the most explicit statements in recent horror: Cecilia destroys the institution that violated her body rather than accept the role assigned to her. VirtueVigil classifies it as a Woke Trap: the Catholic beauty of the first act earns trust that the third act weaponizes.

#7 — Wicked (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 28.42 TRAD: 17.44 MARGIN: -11 WOKE

Genre: Musical • Platform: Theatrical / Peacock

Universal sold Wicked as a family-friendly holiday spectacle with 400 brand partnerships and church-group marketing. The story being sold is a consistent allegory for outsider identity, institutional corruption, and social justice awakening disguised as a splashy musical. Elphaba is persecuted for being different. The system that persecutes her is coded as evil. Glinda is a well-meaning product of that corrupt system who slowly awakens to its injustice. Director Jon M. Chu publicly connected the villain to Donald Trump. Four of the lead cast are openly queer. The LGBTQ+ community has claimed this story for twenty years. The marketing tried to make it feel neutral. The story does not cooperate.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Wicked

#8 — Monkey Man (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 28.0 TRAD: 14.0 MARGIN: -14 WOKE

Genre: Action • Platform: Theatrical / Peacock

Dev Patel spent seven years and sustained real injuries making this John Wick-style revenge thriller set in a fictional Indian city ruled by corrupt Hindu nationalist politicians. Jordan Peele stepped in when Netflix passed and made sure it reached theaters. The political subtext is not subtext: the villain is a thinly veiled Hindu nationalist, the hero comes from the lowest caste, and the climax takes place in a hijra sanctuary. Patel has been explicit in interviews about exactly what he was making. The action genre packaging is effective commercial camouflage for a film that is as explicitly political as any 2024 release. A woke score of 28 reflects messaging that runs through every level of the story.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Monkey Man

#9 — Emilia Perez (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE WOKE: 28.0 TRAD: 6.0 MARGIN: -22 WOKE

Genre: Musical/Crime/Drama • Platform: Netflix

Jacques Audiard's French film about a Mexican cartel boss who transitions to a woman earned 13 Oscar nominations, the most ever for a non-English-language film, and managed to unite both progressive and conservative critics against it for different reasons. GLAAD criticized its portrayal of trans identity. Conservatives objected to its central premise. The Academy celebrated it anyway. The film frames gender transition as liberation and moral rebirth, with the cartel past coded as a male identity to be discarded. The resulting woke score of 28 reflects dense identity-focused content embedded throughout a crime narrative that is too formally inventive to be dismissed as simple agitprop.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Emilia Perez

#10 — Love Lies Bleeding (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 26.0 TRAD: 9.0 MARGIN: -17 WOKE

Genre: Thriller • Platform: Theatrical / MGM+

Rose Glass returned with a surrealist neo-noir starring Kristen Stewart and Katy O'Brien. Stewart plays a gym manager in a violent family environment who falls for a female bodybuilder passing through town. The romance is explicitly lesbian, the relationship is intense and self-destructive, and the film tips into full surrealism by the final act. A24 distributed it. It premiered at Sundance. Critics gave it 94% on Rotten Tomatoes. Glass frames female rage as something mythic and justified, and the male characters in the story are coded uniformly as predatory or ineffectual. The woke score of 26 reflects consistent progressive content throughout, including the relationship framing and the surrealist climax.

#11 — Joker: Folie a Deux (2024)

WOKE LEAN WOKE: 24.5 TRAD: 22.13 MARGIN: -2 WOKE

Genre: Musical/Crime • Platform: Theatrical

Todd Phillips spent $200 million to make a sequel that exists primarily to punish its predecessor's audience for caring about Arthur Fleck. The first Joker worked because it asked a dangerous question with genuine empathy. The sequel exists to declare that empathy undeserved. The musical format, the legal trial structure, and Lady Gaga's Harley Quinn deconstruct the franchise mythology with contempt for the viewers who made the original a cultural phenomenon. The progressive critique of the original Joker's cultural reception is embedded in the film's structure. It grossed $57.5 million domestically against a $200 million budget. The market delivered its verdict.

#12 — Blink Twice (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 22.24 TRAD: 5.88 MARGIN: -16 WOKE

Genre: Thriller • Platform: Theatrical / Amazon Prime Video

Zoe Kravitz made a #MeToo thriller about what it is like to be a woman in proximity to the kind of wealth and power that makes crimes disappear. An island retreat. A perfume that wipes memories. A therapist who facilitates systematic violation. Kravitz frames male power and wealth as inherently predatory, the enabling institutions as complicit, and the women's collective resistance as the only viable response. The film's woke score of 22.24 reflects dense gender-politics content with almost no countervailing traditional material. A technically proficient thriller that knows exactly what it is saying and says it without hesitation throughout.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Blink Twice

#13 — Civil War (2024)

WOKE LEAN WOKE: 22.0 TRAD: 18.0 MARGIN: -4 WOKE

Genre: Action/Drama • Platform: Theatrical / Amazon Prime Video

Alex Garland made a film about a second American Civil War that deliberately refuses to name which political party controls the fascist president or which side the Texas-California alliance represents. That refusal is itself a progressive argument: that presenting political horror without partisan labels is the most honest approach. Both sides receive VirtueVigil flags, but the film's anti-institutional messaging and its framing of the military state as the primary villain push the margin four points into woke territory. One of A24's highest-grossing films ever, and one of the most genuinely debated films in the culture war since its release. The ambiguity is the point, and that ambiguity earns it a place in the top tier of 2024's woke-leaning releases.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Civil War

#14 — Nickel Boys (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 21.84 TRAD: 8.74 MARGIN: -13 WOKE

Genre: Drama • Platform: Theatrical

RaMell Ross adapts Colson Whitehead's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel about a Black teenager wrongfully sent to a Florida reform school in the 1960s, using a radical first-person cinematographic technique that puts viewers inside the protagonist's perspective. The film does not want you to watch the story. It wants you to live inside it. Based on the real Dozier School for Boys where more than 50 boys were killed, the film's systemic racism indictment is rooted in documented historical fact. The woke score of 21.84 reflects the density of racial justice messaging and institutional critique throughout, though the film's technique is so formally inventive that ideological content often feels inseparable from its cinematic approach.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Nickel Boys

#15 — The Apprentice (2024)

WOKE WOKE: 21.0 TRAD: 6.65 MARGIN: -14 WOKE

Genre: Biography/Drama • Platform: Theatrical

Ali Abbasi and Gabriel Sherman made a Trump origin story built around the thesis that everything Donald Trump became was shaped by Roy Cohn's three rules: attack rather than defend, deny everything, and never admit weakness. The film is a sustained progressive argument that the current American political moment was assembled from cynicism and corruption rather than any genuine conviction. Sebastian Stan's Trump and Jeremy Strong's Cohn give committed performances that elevate a film whose ideological agenda is never in question. At a woke score of 21 with almost no traditional content in its scorecard, this is one of the most openly political films of 2024 and one of the least interested in hiding it.

Methodology Note

All scores are generated using the VirtueVigil Woke Score system, which measures the density and intensity of progressive ideological content across multiple categories including gender politics, religious critique, racial messaging, sexual content framing, and institutional critique. The system does not measure quality, entertainment value, or artistic merit. A high score means a film contains a high volume of identifiable progressive messaging relative to its runtime. For full details on how we score, visit our Methodology page.

This list represents every 2024 film reviewed by VirtueVigil as of the publication date. Additional 2024 titles may be reviewed in the future. Scores are final once published and are not adjusted retroactively. For a curated version of this list focusing only on the top 10, see our original Most Woke Movies of 2024 ranking. For comparison across other years, see our 2023, 2025, and 2026 rankings.
